title: Available date and rental cover letters in Australia
excerpt: Unsure what Available Date means, or how to write a rental introduction letter? Starting from how agents actually review applications, this article breaks down the screening criteria behind application details to help you enter key information accurately, write a Cover Letter that fits Australian rental practices, reduce ineffective applications and the risk of rejection, and use Qrent's data tools to approach each application with greater confidence.
content:
**Publication date: 2025-12-26**

**Estimated reading time: 6 minutes**

**Author: Qrent Team**

**Tags: renting in Australia, international student rentals, available date, rental introduction letter, cover letter, Sydney rentals**

---

## I. Background and the Question

On Australia's major rental platforms (such as Realestate, Domain and Qrent), you will often see this field in a property listing:

> Available Date: 10 November 2025

Many international students renting in Australia for the first time have questions:

- Does the available date mean that is the day I can first inspect the property?

- Can I apply in advance?

- The agent has asked me to write a cover letter, but I do not know what to include.

In fact, **the available date is closely connected to application timing and application documents, especially the Cover Letter**.

This article will explain systematically:

- What available date actually means

- When it is most appropriate to submit an application

- The role of a Cover Letter, how to write one, and the reasoning behind preparing the documents

---

## II. What Does Available Date Mean?

In the Australian rental system, **available date means “the date the property is available to move into”**: the time when the landlord expects to be able to hand over the keys and allow the tenant to move in officially.

For example:

> Available Date: 10 November 2025

This means the earliest move-in date for this property is 2025-11-10.

It is especially important to note that:

**available date does not mean “the earliest time you can apply”.**

---

### Qrent's Recommended Application Timing

| Situation | Recommended Approach |
| --- | --- |
| An available date is shown | You can submit an application immediately; most landlords want to confirm a tenant 2–3 weeks in advance |
| The available date is more than 1 month away | You can save the property and set a reminder first |
| The available date has passed | The property is usually already vacant, and you can apply at any time |
| No available date is shown | Confirm with the agent; you can email to ask about the move-in date |

💡 Practical experience shows that:

In Australia, **submitting an application too early (such as 3 months ahead) may instead be considered “too early” and not be given priority**.

---

## III. Why Must You Write a Cover Letter for a Rental Application?

In the Australian rental process, **a Cover Letter (a rental introduction letter) is not merely a formality**.

When an agent or landlord reviews an application, the Cover Letter helps them quickly judge:

> “Whether you are a reliable tenant who follows the rules and can pay rent on time.”

Especially in highly competitive areas, **the Cover Letter is often one of the key factors that sets applications apart**.

---

## IV. The Reasoning and Key Points Behind Writing a Cover Letter

The core goal of a Cover Letter is not “how well it is written”, but that it is **clear, credible and easy to assess**.

### The Main Points to Include Are:

- Who you are and where you study or work

- Why you want to rent this property

- Your stability and sense of responsibility as a tenant

- Whether your ability to pay is clear

The recommended length is **100–150 characters**, using natural language.

---

## V. Where to Enter the Cover Letter and How to Supplement the Documents

On platforms such as Realestate and Domain, the Cover Letter is usually entered in the **“About Me / Cover Letter”** field of the application form.

The main purpose of this section is to **introduce your overall circumstances to the landlord**.

Many applicants get stuck here because they do not know what information to include.

### A Cover Letter Can Emphasise:

- Whether you are tidy and keep a regular routine

- Whether you do not smoke, do not keep pets and do not hold parties

- Whether you can pay rent on time and stay for a stable, long-term period

Below the Cover Letter, you can usually **upload attachments**.

As long as you do not violate the platform's rules, you can add any documents that strengthen your “reliability”, for example:

- A student visa or COE

- Proof of savings

- Screenshots of previous rent or utility bills

---

## VI. How Should You Complete Other Key Sections of the Application Form?

### 1. Address History (Residential History)

You need to enter **your residential addresses for the past two years**.

- If you have previously rented in Australia, you can enter your former landlord's contact details after obtaining their permission

- The platform will email your former landlord to ask about your conduct as a tenant

- If you previously lived in China and did not rent, you can enter your family home address

- For the landlord's contact details, you can enter your parents' information and complete the questionnaire yourself

---

### 2. Employment (Work Situation)

- If you have a job, enter your employment information

- If you do not currently have a job (such as a full-time international student), you can truthfully select “No employment”

- If you are concerned that the landlord may doubt your ability to pay, you can provide proof of funds in other sections

---

### 3. Income (Income Situation)

- Applicants who work can upload a payslip

- International students can upload screenshots of living allowance transfers from their parents

- The core goal is to **prove that you can continue paying the rent**

---

### 4. Identity Documents (Proof of Identity)

You can upload documents containing your identity information, for example:

- A passport

- A driving licence

- A medical insurance card

---

### 5. Emergency Contact (Emergency Contact Person)

Enter a reliable family member or friend.

---

## VII. Explanation of the Application Document Scoring System (Common Platform Approach)

Most platforms use **a points-based document review system**, commonly structured as follows:

### Category A Primary Documents (At Least 40 Points Required)

- Passport (40 points)

- Student card / birth certificate / driving licence, etc.

### Category B Supporting Documents (At Least 40 Points Required)

- Health insurance card, visa, proof of address

- Utility bills, current lease

- Parental guarantee or related proof

### Proof of Income (At Least 20 Points Required)

- Payslip / employment agreement

- Proof of savings (from China or Australia)

💡 **Important note**:

It is common not to have utility bills when renting for the first time. **As long as you reach the required points within that category, you do not need to force yourself to provide a particular item**.

---

## VIII. How Does Qrent Help Improve Your Application Success Rate?

Qrent provides the following support to help international students complete applications more efficiently:

- Editable English Cover Letter templates

- Available date and application timing tips

- Area average rent analysis to assess whether the asking price is reasonable

- AI property scoring to assess competition and value for money

Qrent's core advice is:

> The applicant a landlord favours most is not “the person who applies earliest”, but “the person who is most fully prepared”.

---

## IX. Key Points

- available date = the date the property is available to move into

- You can usually submit an application 2–3 weeks in advance

- The Cover Letter is a key document landlords use to assess reliability

- Attachments and supporting documents can significantly strengthen your application

- First-time renters do not need to worry about not having every document; they only need to satisfy the scoring criteria
